mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 4.0% signals strong labor market conditions that increase consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages indicate robust consumer demand expansion, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) creates a stable monetary environment that supports equity valuations, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 2.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects expanding manufacturing output that correlates with stronger corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when INDPRO rises from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth exceeding 0.5% year-over-year signals robust economic expansion that increases corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint conditions of strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 0.3% monthly) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicate a tight labor market that fuels consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.3% and UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) combined with strong job growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly) creates a virtuous cycle of wage growth and consumer spending that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.3%.
